tools_helpful.evidence: session-log turns 1-3: scaffolding and bootstrap completed, produced MIGRATION-MAPPING.md, and rewrote the files it could see.
session-log turn 8: the csproj and navigation anchors supplied concrete manifest and frame-wiring guidance.
session-log turn 28: residue, mapping, manifest, build, and startup checks all completed with PASS.
session-log turns 14-27: project-qualified dotnet commands exposed compiler/deployment errors and ultimately launched the app.

tools_problematic.problem: It recursively copied only files physically below the project directory and ignored explicit csproj Include/Link items outside that directory.
tools_problematic.evidence: session-log turn 2 reported only 9 copied files and zero XAML TODOs; NumberFormatting.csproj declares linked MainPage, scenario XAML, shared styles, code, and assets.

tools_problematic.problem: The installed CLI has no build subcommand.
tools_problematic.evidence: session-log turn 29: 'build' was not matched and the CLI listed run/package commands but no build command.

tool_limitations.limitation: The agent did not use it and instead left dotnet run active for 180 seconds.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: No tooling change: the skill already makes Test-AppLaunch.ps1 the required launch command.

doc_errors.where: SKILL.md Step 3, build command discipline, and final build
doc_errors.wrong: The skill recommended winapp build even though the installed winapp CLI has no build subcommand.
doc_errors.correct: Compile with dotnet build <path-to-csproj>; use Test-AppLaunch.ps1 for launch diagnostics.

doc_errors.where: SKILL.md shell conversion and MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md navigationview-frame-wiring
doc_errors.wrong: The skill mapped an SDK-sample ListView/Frame shell to NavigationView/Frame despite its own no-redesign rule and despite SplitView, ListView, and Frame being supported.
doc_errors.correct: Add only the desktop Window host; preserve supported shell controls and use NavigationView only when it is already present or an unsupported shell requires it.

errors_encountered.error: Couldn't find a project to run.
errors_encountered.root_cause: dotnet run was invoked from the parent app directory rather than the child project directory and no --project argument was supplied.
errors_encountered.fix: Run dotnet with --project pointing to NumberFormatting.csproj.

errors_encountered.error: CS0101/CS0102 duplicate Scenario and FEATURE_NAME, followed by WMC0909/WMC1111/WMC9999.
errors_encountered.root_cause: The agent recreated declarations in MainPage.xaml.cs while retaining the copied SampleConfiguration.cs declarations, leaving x:DataType unresolved during XAML compilation.
errors_encountered.fix: Removed the duplicate declarations from SampleConfiguration.cs.

errors_encountered.error: WMC0503: Compiled Bindings cannot be processed in Property Element form.
errors_encountered.root_cause: The newly authored NavigationView used x:Bind as a property-element child.
errors_encountered.fix: Moved the binding to MenuItemsSource="{x:Bind Scenarios}".

errors_encountered.error: WMC0035: Duplication assignment to the Content property of NavigationView.
errors_encountered.root_cause: MenuItemsSource was inserted as text inside the NavigationView content after a Header property element, so XAML treated it as a second content assignment.
errors_encountered.fix: Moved Header and MenuItemsSource to attributes on NavigationView.

errors_encountered.error: CS8629 nullable value type may be null on ParseDouble(...).Value.
errors_encountered.root_cause: The migrated project enabled nullable analysis while the UWP source dereferenced nullable parse results.
errors_encountered.fix: Added a typed helper that throws if parsing returns null.

errors_encountered.root_cause: The UWP manifest was copied without its linked shared assets, and its UWP desktop-incompatible shape was retained.
errors_encountered.fix: Reconciled the manifest to scaffold assets, Windows.Desktop, $targetentrypoint$, and runFullTrust.

errors_encountered.root_cause: The migration skill documented a nonexistent CLI subcommand.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: The agent searched generated obj XAML, manually recreated eight XAML files, and required four compile-fix iterations.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: 18 turns from source discovery through the fourth XAML/compiler correction.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: The bootstrap omitted csproj-linked shared XAML/code/assets, forcing manual reconstruction; the shell guidance also encouraged NavigationView instead of preserving supported controls.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: The agent reconstructed pages from generated XAML and fixed each compiler error individually.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Resolve explicit Include/Link items during bootstrap and state that supported source shells must not be modernized.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: The first successful build failed package registration on a missing splash asset.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: One failed launch and one manifest rewrite.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: Linked shared assets were absent and the existing csproj anchor was not applied before launch.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: The manifest was rebuilt around scaffold assets and desktop package requirements.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Bootstrap linked Content items and follow the existing manifest checklist before first launch.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: The requested final build command failed immediately.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: One unrecovered command failure at the end of the session.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: The skill named a winapp subcommand that does not exist.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Not resolved in the trial; the prior validator's dotnet build had already passed.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Replace every winapp build instruction with dotnet build <path-to-csproj>.

missing_tooling.need: Bootstrap discovery and copying of explicit csproj Include/Link items.
missing_tooling.would_have_saved: Manual obj-tree discovery, eight hand-authored XAML files, missing shared assets, multiple XAML compiler retries, and the resulting visual redesign.
